title: Touch target expansion and virtualized-table row-snap QA for Safari/Firefox mobile
creator: Asha Menon
description: Objective: run a focused cross-browser QA sweep on compact/compact-dense button hit areas, chart overlay stacking/positioning when sticky containers are present, and virtualized table row snap/scroll behavior on mobile Safari and Firefox Android. Background: several customer reports and internal telemetry show inconsistent hitboxes and occasional 1px shifting when the console's charts overlap sticky headers. Virtualized table regressions surfaced after virtualization upgrade (ENG-4123). Goal is to produce reproducible steps, severity classification, and a prioritized set of design fixes or engineering tickets. Links: Confluence spec - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UIKIT/Touch+Targets+and+Virtualized+Tables, Design Figma - https://www.figma.com/file/UiKit/Redwood-UI-Kit-Access, GH PR referencing virtualization change - https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/1589.
steps_to_reproduce: Open Console on iPhone 13 (iOS 17.2) Safari in responsive view, sign in to demo org and navigate to Routes > Topology where charts + sticky header present
Toggle compact density and attempt to tap compact action buttons inside table rows while scrolling quickly
Observe tap misses or delayed focus due to 1) reduced hit area and 2) nearest interactive element receiving pointer event
Repeat on Firefox Nightly for Android (Pixel 7) with touch throttling enabled
In virtualization-heavy pages (1000+ rows) perform fast fling scrolls and watch for snapped row misalignment and stale hover states when virtualization re-renders
Open network throttling 3G and repeat to check event ordering and pointer capture race conditions
findings: Compact button icons reduced to 20x20 visual size while CSS touch padding collapsed to 6px, violating WCAG touch guidance
iOS Safari treats overlapping sticky z-indexed chart overlays as higher priority for pointer events in certain stacking contexts, causing taps on underlying buttons to be swallowed
Firefox Android produced consistent 'ghost tap' where the virtualized list re-rendered a different DOM node at the tapped index before pointerup fired
Virtualized table uses absolute positioning with fractional pixel rounding; on high-DPR displays this leads to 0.5px offsets and perceived 1px jumps during fast scrolls
Regression correlates with ENG-4123 (virtualization refactor) and a recent CSS token change reducing interactive padding (DES-81420 style token rollup)
severity_and_customer_impact: medium - affects mobile-first flows and developer productivity in Console; some enterprise customers reported frequent misses when triaging traces on mobile which increases task time. Not blocking account access, but high annoyance and UX friction.
proposed_fixes: Design: increase minimum hit area for compact buttons to 40px square via touch-padding utility token (token: touch.min-size = 40) and map to components without increasing visual size
Engineering: add pointer-events:none to chart overlay masks when overlays are decorative; add explicit pointer capture behavior for active buttons to avoid stacking-context steals
Engineering: introduce 0.5px snap compensation in virtualization layer to align fractional positions on high-DPR; debounce re-rendering for 150ms during fast flings to avoid ghost-tap races
QA: add end-to-end tests on BrowserStack for iOS Safari + Firefox Android that assert minimum tap success rate for compact mode (target >= 95% for 10 runs)
Docs: update UI Kit accessibility guidelines for compact density and include code snippets for hit area utility
